text:
A: Hi. Erm, can you hear me?
B: Yes. Hi. I am Jurgita.
A: I'm Bethany. Sorry, my cat might walk across the screen at some point.
B: Is okay. I saw him in your photo, on the sofa.
A: Yeah, that's Biscuit. He's sort of in charge. Erm, where are you, sorry?
B: Wakefield. Yorkshire.
A: Oh, nice. I'm in Basingstoke.
B: Okay.
A: Yeah. Erm. What do you do, like for work?
B: Senior care assistant. In care home, for old people. Twelve-hour shifts, mostly days. I did three long days this week already, so I am knackered, honestly.
A: Three twelve-hour days? That's a lot.
B: Is normal. But they change the rota again without asking anyone. Every week the same. Manager puts it on the board, and you find out you're working Sunday. And some people, they always get the good shifts, and they don't do half the work, you know.
A: That sounds really frustrating, sorry. Do you like the actual job, though, like with the residents?
B: Residents are okay. Some are lovely. One lady calls me Margaret all week, I don't know who is Margaret. I just say yes, love, is Margaret. Is easier.
A: Aw, that's kind of sweet actually.
B: Paperwork is not sweet. Care notes, every little thing, at end of shift. That I don't like. What do you do?
A: Erm, I work on an IT service desk, at an insurance company. Second-line support. So people ring up when their laptop's broken or they're locked out, and I sort it.
B: People are angry when they ring?
A: Sometimes, yeah. But I sort of don't mind. If you're calm with them they calm down usually. I'd rather that than sitting in meetings, to be honest.
B: Yes. Meetings, I hate also. Team leader asked me do I want to be team leader. More paperwork, little bit more money. No thanks.
A: Yeah, I'd hate that. Being a manager, I mean. I'd rather just fix things.
B: Exactly.
A: Yeah.
B: You have a cross. In photo. You are Catholic?
A: Oh, erm, no, Church of England. I go every few weeks, I sit at the back mostly. Sorry, are you?
B: Catholic, yes. From Lithuania. I go to Mass in Leeds, Polish and Lithuanian, at Christmas and Easter. More for my mum, when she phones and asks, did you go. I say yes.
A: Ha, yeah. My mum's a bit like that too. Do you get back to Lithuania much?
B: Once a year, two weeks in summer. And Tenerife sometimes, all-inclusive. Pool, nothing else.
A: That sounds nice, actually. I really need to renew my passport, I keep saying I will.
B: Do it on the internet, is quick. And you know, I got new bag in the sale last week, TK Maxx, Michael Kors, forty pound. Proper bargain.
A: Forty? That's really good. I never find anything in TK Maxx, I just sort of wander round.
B: You have to go Tuesday, when they put new stock out. Tuesday morning, before—
